items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S2359

SPONSOR: BROUK
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act directing the commissioner of mental health to establish a mater-
nal mental health workgroup to study and issue recommendations related
to maternal mental health and perinatal and postpartum mood and anxiety
disorders; and providing for the repeal of such provision upon expira-
tion thereof

 
PURPOSE:

The purpose of this legislation is to establish a maternal mental health
workgroup within the office of mental health to study and issue recom-
mendations that will improve the impacts that maternal mental health
disorders have on women and birthing people, children and families.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 of this bill requires the Commissioner of the Office of Mental
Health to establish within the Office of Mental Health, a maternal
mental health workgroup that would consist of the Office of Children and
Family Services, the Department of Health and other relevant stakehold-
ers.

Section 2 of this bill requires that none of the workgroup members
receive compensation for their services as members of the workgroup, but
receive reimbursement for the actual expenses incurred in the perform-
ance of the duties of the workgroup. The bill also outlines that
reimbursement for historically underrepresented members on the workgroup
may include but not be limited to, childcare, travel, meals and lodging.

Section 3 of this bill requires the workgroup to study maternal mental
health disorders and submit a final report containing all findings and
recommendations to the governor, the temporary president of the
senate,the speaker of the assembly, the commissioner of the office of
mental health, the commissioner of the office of children and family
services, the commissioner of the department of health, the minority
leader of the senate and the minority leader of the assembly on or
before December 31,2022.

Section 4 of this bill sets forth the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

This bill would direct the Office of Mental Health to establish a mater-
nal mental health workgroup. The workgroup would study and issue recom-
mendations on maternal mental health disorders. It would identify
under-represented and vulnerable populations, risk factors, successful
screening and treatment methods, as well as make recommendations on
policy initiatives and funding models.

Creating this workgroup is a necessary step towards gaining a clearer
understanding of New York's maternal mental health policies, programs,
and funding sources. It will help identify and evaluate the best prac-
tices for reducing the racial and ethnic disparities that presently
exist in maternal mental health and help improve the negative impacts
associated with these disorders.Section 2500-k of the Public Health Law
defines the term "maternal depression" as a wide range of emotional and
psychological reactions one may experience during pregnancy or after
childbirth. These reactions may include but are not limited to, feelings
of despair or extreme guilt, prolonged sadness, lack of energy, diffi-
culty concentrating, fatigue, extreme changes in appetite, and thoughts
of suicide or of harming the baby. Maternal depression may include
prenatal depression, the "baby blues," postpartum depression, or post-
partum psychosis - the severest form. Maternal depression can create
bonding issues between a gestation- al parent and their baby, contribute
to sleep and feeding problems, and cause emotional, developmental and
verbal complications in children. These children may then need greater
remediation, intervention and resources later in development.

According to both the Center for Disease Control (CDC) and the National
Alliance on Mental Illness (NAMI), maternal depression affects one in
eight new mothers, but the risk is significantly higher for new mothers
of color. Notably, while Black women are three times more likely to
experience maternal depression, they are the least less likely to
receive help. It is estimated that over half of the instances of mater-
nal depression in women of color go unreported.  And current screening
methods may be less effective at detecting maternal depression in black
and brown women, as well as in nonbinary and transmasculine gestational
parents.

If we are able to better diagnose and treat the tens of thousands of
mothers and families affected by maternal mental health disorders
depression annually, we will uplift not only these women but the growing
families who depend on them across the state.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2021-22: passed Senate. Returned to Senate. Vetoed, Memo .80

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

To be determined.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.

summary: Directs the commissioner of mental health to establish a maternal mental health workgroup to study and issue recommendations related to maternal mental health and perinatal and postpartum mood and anxiety disorders; identifies underrepresented and vulnerable populations and risk factors in the state for maternal mental health disorders that may occur during pregnancy and through the first postpartum year.
title: Establishes a maternal mental health workgroup
